articles.title: All Blacks great Beauden Barrett close to Bristol move
articles.summary: New Zealand great Beauden Barrett is close to agreeing a deal to join Bristol Bears in what would be one of the highest-profile signings in Prem history.
body: The 35-year-old, who is widely considered one of the best All Blacks of all time, won his 150th international cap in Saturday's defeat by England in Twickenham.
It is understood he is in discussions about joining Bristol on a two-year deal after the 2027 Rugby World Cup.
Barrett is also the subject of interest from clubs in France as he plots the final stages of his illustrious career. An announcement on his future is expected in the coming weeks.
Bristol have yet to comment on the situation, but sources close to the deal feel the Bears are in a strong position to sign the 2015 World Cup winner.

articles.title: Khawaja 'hurt' by 'personal attacks' from Cummins in sandpaper denials
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja has told the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast that he was "hurt" by Pat Cummins' "personal attacks" on him as the Australia Test captain explosively disputed his claims that every member of the side was aware of the use of sandpaper in 2018.
body: Khawaja made the allegations in his autobiography Sabr and they have since been backed up by David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of the players, along with then-skipper Steve Smith, who were slapped with bans following the ball-tampering plot in South Africa.

Cummins, part of the Australia bowling attack on that tour eight years ago, insisted he was not privy to the scheme when he and fellow quicks Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, as well as spinner Nathan Lyon, released a joint-statement in 2021.
He then categorially denied knowledge earlier this month in a 68-minute press conference in which he accused Khawaja of being "casual" with people's lives.
Khawaja said in a chat with Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain: "It was the most surprised I've been for a long time. I wasn't expecting that [from Cummins] whatsoever.

articles.title: Dottin out to 'free ball' after historic WBBL decision
articles.summary: Brisbane's Sarah Glenn bowls to an empty set of stumps to dismiss Melbourne Renegade's Deandra Dottin after she is deemed too slow to reach the crease and face her first delivery.
body: A bizarre dismissal in the Women's Big Bash saw Brisbane Heat's Sarah Glenn bowling to an empty set of stumps, external after Melbourne Renegades new batter Deandra Dottin was ruled to have taken too long to face the delivery.

Experienced West Indies all-rounder Dottin walked out to bat, following the dismissal of Georgia Wareham, with her equipment in disarray and proceeded to adjust her helmet and begin putting on her gloves after arriving in the middle.

Rules introduced before the 2021 WBBL season to speed up play state that an incoming batter must be ready to face - or the non-striker to receive - the next delivery within 75 seconds of a dismissal or retirement.
The umpires adjudged Dottin to have exceeded this time limit and instructed her to stand aside from stumps, while awarding Glenn a free ball.

articles.title: Murrell flourishing at high-flying Falkirk after 'random' move
articles.summary: Jacob Murrell took a big step out of his comfort zone leaving the United States for Falkirk and is enjoying a blistering run of form in Scotland, if not the food.
body: "It was completely random," is how Jacob Murrell describes his summer switch from DC United to Falkirk.
Now the 22 year-old American is the joint-leading scorer in the Scottish Premiership, with eight goals from 11 starts.
His tremendous form has helped Falkirk surge up the table, with six successive victories taking them from 11th to third place.
"I was looking for more minutes as a young player and Falkirk kind of came out of nowhere," he explained. "They called my agent and a week later I was in Scotland.

articles.title: The NFL's biggest game of the season is here - it could break records
articles.summary: It has become an era-defining rivalry in the NFL, and now the Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills will meet yet again in the biggest game of the regular season on one of football's most-watched stages.
body: Patrick Mahomes and Josh Allen will face off for the 11th time when they headline the NFL's Thanksgiving schedule on Thursday night, live on Sky Sports from 1.20am in the early hours of Friday.
Once more they are positioned neck and neck at the forefront of the NFL's playoff race, once more they will trade the greatness that has governed football for the best part of a decade.

Together they have forged modern football's answer to Tom Brady vs Peyton Manning. Two generational quarterbacks, dictating one another's story, time and time again, although Allen would prefer if the outcome had been a little more even by now.

Mahomes, the driver of a Chiefs dynasty and so often the AFC's Super Bowl gateway; and Allen, the starved nearly man banging down on the Championship door only to see dominant talent blunted by his Kansas City counterpart.

articles.title: Ice hockey federation appeals against Russia ban ruling
articles.summary: The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) will appeal to the Swiss Federal Tribunal against a Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) ruling to reinstate Russia in next year's World Championship.
body: Russia has been banned from competing in IIHF events since the invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, with the sport's global governing body ruling earlier this year that the exclusion would continue.

On 30 October, Cas upheld appeals from the Russian Ice Hockey Federation against the ban, claiming arguments made by the IIHF "citing safety, security and other concerns" were "not supported by sufficient evidence".
The IIHF has cited alleged undisclosed links to Russia from two of the three Cas panel members in its appeal to the Swiss Federal Tribunal.
"The decision is based on concerns around the independence and impartiality of two of the three arbitrators on the CAS Panel," an IIHF statement said.

articles.title: Sterling given suspended jail sentence for dangerous driving
articles.summary: Former England player Raheem Sterling has been given a suspended 12-month jail sentence for dangerous driving and possession of nitrous oxide after a crash involving a Lamborghini on the motorway.
body: Sterling pleaded guilty at Basingstoke Magistrates' Court in September to driving a Lamborghini Urus dangerously on the M25, the M3, the A327 and Minley Road before he crashed on May 28. The sentence is suspended for 18 months.
He has also been handed a two-year driving ban and must undertake 100 hours of unpaid community work. Sterling will have to re-take a driving test to hold a licence.
The 31-year-old admitted possession of six nitrous oxide cannisters for wrongful inhalation, a class C drug, and failing to provide a specimen.
Mitigating factors taken into account by District Judge Kirsty Allman were Sterling's guilty plea, that he had no prior convictions and a clean driving licence prior to his arrest in May.

articles.title: Sterling's career was defined by comebacks - this could be one too many
articles.summary: There once existed a time where Raheem Sterling was an unstoppable force. A player with a uniquely abstract running style, he still somehow evoked effortless poise when moving with the ball. A glider across a pitch.
body: Sterling played a dominant role in Manchester City's most definitive era, one led by the greatest tactical mind of a generation. But this forward exuded genius of his own.

A teenage prodigy that climbed his way to the very top of the game, Sterling was driven by his origin story rather than burdened by it. At his height, he drew comparisons to Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo as a player capable of "winning the race", according to Barcelona great Xavi, to become the world's next best thing.

His 82 international caps pointed towards a boundless trajectory; England's most impactful player on their run to the Euro 2020 final. In an alternate world, he would still be part of Thomas Tuchel's England set-up now, the coach being a key advocate for the move that took Sterling from Man City to Chelsea in 2022. He was still only 27.

For a player that burst onto the scene an entire decade before, Sterling's status and authority at the top was enduring. He made his Liverpool debut at 17 and his senior England bow 24 days before his 18th birthday. The peak of his Premier League powers ran parallel with many of the game's elite performers. That should not be forgotten.

articles.title: Ernie Els Tells Tiger Woods It’s Time To Ride In 2027
articles.summary: Ernie Els has sent a clear message to Tiger Woods: the time to play the Champions Tour is now. The South African legend believes 2027 is the perfect year for Woods to join the senior circuit. This comes after Woods missed his first full year of eligibility due to injuries and a car crash.
body: The Big Easy spoke on the 5 Clubs podcast to share his thoughts on Woods’ potential return. Els has been part of the over-50s tour since 2020, so he knows the ropes. He sees Woods as a key player who would bring huge energy to the group. Sitting at home with injuries is not good for anyone, especially a competitor like Woods. Els said, “It’s great to see Tiger teeing it up,” when discussing the upcoming Hero World Challenge.

One major reason Els pushes for a 2027 debut is the relief a golf cart provides. Players on the Champions Tour are allowed to use buggies during competition. This rule change could make a huge difference for Woods, who has battled severe leg and back issues. If permitted by the regulations, he has already stated he would gladly use a cart. Els told the podcast, “I hope next year’s going to be the year he decides to maybe come out and play a few, and ride around in a cart if he’s allowed to.”

articles.title: AJ Dybantsa: “I’ve Been A Celtics Fan Since I Came Out The Womb”
articles.summary: Washington Wizards rookie AJ Dybantsa has been a Boston Celtics fan for as long as he can remember, making his first NBA matchup against his childhood team a special occasion.
body: After Washington’s 131–116 NBA Cup loss at Capital One Arena on Tuesday, Dybantsa reflected on growing up in Massachusetts and following generations of Celtics stars.

“I’ve been a Celtics fan since I came out of the womb. I was born in Boston. I’ve been going to Boston Celtics games since I was two years old, wearing Kevin Garnett’s jersey, Paul Pierce’s jersey, to Isaiah Thomas, all the way to Tatum and Brown when they won that chip.”

The Brockton native’s connection to Boston covers several chapters of the franchise’s recent history. He grew up watching established champions, followed Thomas’ memorable run and later saw Tatum and Brown bring another championship to the Celtics.

Now, the No. 1 pick is competing against the franchise he once watched from the stands. His first meeting took place in Washington, but he expects the emotions to rise another level when the Wizards travel to Boston.

articles.title: Hamilton: “I Don’t Want That” in Response to Leclerc’s Penalty—Radio Revealed
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton told his race engineer he didn’t want Charles Leclerc to be penalized for their Las Vegas GP collision, with the focus on scoring more points. It was another clash between the Ferrari drivers in the F1 Las Vegas GP.
body: When battling the McLaren pair, Hamilton was cleared by Oscar Piastri in the lead-up to Turn 7. Leclerc tried a move on the inside of the Brit, but made contact, sending the seven-time F1 champion into a spin on the tarmac run-off.

The stewards handed Leclerc a 10s time penalty, as they felt the Monégasque was not alongside Hamilton enough to warrant space. Leclerc finished 10th after the penalty, helping the Brit move up to seventh, but Ferrari lost crucial points to rivals.

It has now emerged that Hamilton didn’t want Leclerc to be penalized. An untelevised radio exchange highlights the aftermath of the incident. There was no radio communication between the Brit and his race engineer, Carlo Santi, after the spin.

Eventually, with eight laps to go, Santi informed him about the penalty, and Hamilton’s immediate response was that he didn’t want it. Hamilton was in the mindset that a penalty would mean a points loss for Ferrari, which he didn’t wish upon his F1 team.

articles.title: 5 WWE Stars Who Could Be Ethan Page’s Next IC Title Challenger, Including Dragon Lee
articles.summary: Ethan Page is finding ways to keep his gold, even if they are not pretty. Page made his first defense of the Men’s Intercontinental Championship on Raw in Wichita on Monday, beating AAA World Cruiserweight Champion Rey Fenix.
body: Page won the title earlier this month, beating Chad Gable on Raw for his first championship on the main roster. He targeted Gable’s neck throughout the match and escaped an ankle lock by kicking Gable into an exposed turnbuckle before hitting the Ego-Plex.
Page has made enemies along the way, and he will not be short on challengers in the weeks ahead. With that in mind, here are five WWE stars who could be next in line for the gold.

Fenix has the most personal reason to want another shot. Going after a luchador’s mask is one of the most disrespectful things a wrestler can do, and Page used it to win. A rematch writes itself. Fenix could ask for a stipulation that keeps Page from cheating his way out again, and a win would give him a major singles title on the main roster to go with his AAA gold.
Gable never got a fair rematch for the title he lost. Page went after his neck to win it, and Gable’s attempt to get back into the title picture ended when Fenix pinned him.

articles.title: Rams vs. Packers prediction: Can Green Bay find continue success with deep ball? Will L.A. overcome injuries?
articles.summary: Micah Parsons makes his season debut for Green Bay as an injury-depleted Los Angeles offense leans on its ground attack in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve showdown
body: In the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve NFL game, the Los Angeles Rams play host to the Green Bay Packers.

The Rams enter this game coming off their bye week, and they are incredibly banged up on offense. Puka Nacua is likely out for the year, as is Terrance Ferguson, after they each underwent surgery on lower-body injuries. Davante Adams remains out with his hamstring injury as well. The Rams will need their defense and their running backs to carry the day against a tough Packers team.

Green Bay is also coming off the bye, but is getting healthier for this game as Micah Parsons will make his season debut after tearing his ACL toward the tail end of last season. Parsons returning to the fold provides a significant boost to what has already been a good defense under Jonathan Gannon, and the offense remains one of the league's most explosive units with Jordan Love targeting Christian Watson and Matthew Golden down the field.
Will the Rams hold off the Packers at home, or will Green Bay pull off the upset? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.
